GraphLiteral\t4253052168.en:
Common Name: Enigmasaur
Species: Proteus mutabilis
Time: Unknown
Diet: Insectivore
Temperament: Highly adaptable

Wild 

Increasingly, I find myself struggling to describe the impossible. Until I saw one of these oversized chameleons steal the shape of a nearby Direwolf, I'm not sure I would have believed such an animal could exist. The creature I'm calling an 'Enigmasaur' didn't just appear to become vulpine in response to the Direwolf... it fully transformed into a wolf, enough to be accepted by others and even hunt with its new pack until it could split off and resume its true form and behavior.

Domesticated 

Once you know what to look for, you might be able to tell which of the local fauna is really an Enigmasaur in disguise. And if you can manage to tame one, you'll add a living Swiss Army knife to your stable. Impress your target by showing it that you've tamed one of the same creatures it's currently mimicking. Repeat this process as it cycles through multiple forms, until you demonstrate your goodwill.

Once you teach your Enigmasaur several forms to pull from its morphic memory, it can retain each creature's useful traits regardless of whichever shape it's currently taken. For example, even after it drops the form of a Pulmonoscorpius to become a Rex, its attacks will stun prey as if it still had a stinger. And returning to its own body will give it access to all of those learned abilities at once! Truly a riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma…

GraphLiteral\t2814358082.en:
Common Name: Giga

Species: Giganotosaurus furiosa

Time: Late Cretaceous

Diet: Carnivore

Temperament: Wrathful

 

Wild

Somehow, this monster's gotten even scarier since I first saw one sink its teeth into a giant ape. Wounding a Giganotosaurus drives it into a berserker rage, and it only becomes tougher to beat the worse it gets hurt. Now, though, it seems to be able to share a measure of its fighting fury with allies in the heat of battle... provided they can stay out of its warpath.

You should be aware that the Giga has new ways of dealing with anyone or anything that manages to dodge its gnashing jaws. It will stomp its feet and slam its tail down hard to smash and scatter attackers at its rear or underfoot.


Domesticated

Breaking one of these behemoths won't be easy. Even if you can get a Giga's attention by killing alpha-level threats, you'll still have an omega-level fight to survive. Let the Giga exhaust itself attacking you, then fight back to provoke its rage. Hang in there long enough to wear the enraged Giga down, and you might just be able to subdue it.

It's more than worth the mortal danger to win this war-beast to your cause. Just aim your Giga at the adversary, and jump clear as its terrible rage flares up. Keep a safe distance, and you'll feel its gigantic ferocity embolden you & your allies to tear through enemy forces together!

GraphLiteral\t1349263401.en:
Common name:
Therizinosaur
Species: Therizinosaurus multiensis
Time: Late Cretaceous
Diet: Herbivore
Temperament: Territorial

Wild
Like several other creatures on the ARKs, Therizinosaurus multiensis seems to be adjusting to our presence. It will even give interlopers a couresy warning before attacking. The beast's newfound tolerance works both ways, as tribes no longer see its encroaching populations as an existential threat. That said, a provoked Therizino is more dangerous than ever.

From a safe distance you'll notice a Therizino adapted to delicate foraging will flash longer, sharper claws, while the rippers of a power-harvester get worn and chipped. Get too close, and whichever style of claws it has will tear into you with the same vicious double-swipe attack.

Domesticated
We're lucky that it's still easy to tame a Therizino. Sedate one into submission and feed it enough, and it'll eventually fall into line. A moounted Therizino turns out to be more clever and agile than you'd expect, for such a big creature. It can turn on a dime, and hop, onto or over obstacles that'd stop and Allo or Rex in their tracks.

You'd be wise to enlist a Therizino's help in your tribe's fight for survival. It's a reliable and tireless harvester and those same reaping blades, are formidable weapons. Saddle one up for the firece protection it gives a rider from attackers and would-be predators.
